Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:10:1.hebrew: שור הבר - דומה לחיה, ואם מגדלו בביתו — הולך למדברות ומטעה החיות לבא אחריו. ויש בהן גזל מפני דרכי שלום, שמביא אותן מן הביברין. והא דקרי ליה בהמה — כמאן דאמר מין בהמה הוא. ופלוגתייהו לענין התרת חלבו וכיסוי הדם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:10:1.english: Wild ox - It resembles an undomesticated animal; and if one raises it in his home, it goes to the wilderness and entices the wild animals to follow it. And there is [an element of] robbery with regard to them on account of the ways of peace, when he brings them from [other people's] enclosures. And that which [the baraita] refers to it as a domesticated animal is in accordance with the one who says that it is a species of domesticated animal. And their dispute pertains to the permissibility of its fat and the covering of the blood.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:11:1.hebrew: חמסן - יהיב דמי, אלא שאין רצון הבעלים למכור:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:11:1.english: One who forces transactions - He gives money, but it is not the owner's wish to sell.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:12:1.hebrew: דאוריי' הוא - אל תשת רשע עד. ובמסכת גיטין (דף נט:) תנן: מציאת חרש, שוטה וקטן יש בהן גזל מפני דרכי שלום, שלא יתקוטט אביו או קרוביו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:12:1.english: [A robber] is [disqualified] by Torah law - [As the Sages expound Exodus 23:1:] “Do not appoint a wicked person as a witness.” And in tractate Gittin (59b) we learned: With regard to an item found by a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor, [taking] it is considered robbery for the sake of the ways of peace, so that his father or his relatives do not quarrel.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:13:1.english: Ultimately they take money - And they transgress a rabbinic enactment on account of coveting money.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:13:2.english: Disqualified them - For they are suspected of taking payment and testifying falsely.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:14:1.hebrew: כיון דחזו דחטפי - ושקלי. כלומר, דאפי' דמי קא יהבי, אתי לידי גזלנות; כלומר, שהיה קשה לבעלים למכור, ובעל כרחן חוטפין וזורקין המעות לפניהם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:14:1.english: Once they saw that they snatch - And take [them]. That is to say, even though they pay money, it comes to robbery; that is to say, that it was difficult for the owners to sell, and against their will they snatch [the items] and throw the money before them.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:15:1.english: Collectors - Officials whom the king appointed to collect the tax, the king's portion, the poll tax, and the produce tax from their fellow Jews.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:16:1.hebrew: אקראי בעלמא - מה שהבהמה נכנסת לשדות של אחרים ורועה — אקראי הוא, ואין הרועה מתכוין לכך:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:16:1.english: Merely incidental - That the animal enters the fields of others and grazes is [merely] incidental, and the shepherd does not intend for this.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:16:2.english: Extra - More than the fixed amount.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:18:1.english: In Eretz Yisrael - [They] are treated more stringently because of the settlement of Eretz Yisrael.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:18:2.hebrew: מגדלין איתמר - שמגדלין אותם בבתיהם, ואפי' הכי בארץ ישראל פסולין מגדלי בהמה דקה, דעבידא דמשמטא ורהטא לתוך השדות. אבל גסה לא משתמטא, ואפשר לנוטרה. אבל רועה שמרען בחוץ באפר של ישוב — אפי' בהמה גסה פסול, שנכנסת בשדה של אחרים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:18:2.english: That was stated with regard to those who raise [animals] - That they raise them in their homes; and even so, in Eretz Yisrael those who raise small livestock are disqualified, as it is prone to slip away and run into the fields. But large [livestock] does not slip away, and it is possible to guard it. But a shepherd who grazes them outside in pastureland near a settlement — even [with] large livestock he is disqualified, as it enters into the field of others.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:19:1.hebrew: ה"נ מסתברא - דרועה בהמה גסה פסול:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:19:1.english: This too stands to reason - That a herder of large livestock is disqualified:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:19:2.hebrew: נאמנין עלי שלשה רועי בקר - מכלל דאי לא קבלינהו עליה, לא מהימני:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:19:2.english: Three cattle herders are trusted for me - By inference, if he did not accept them upon himself, they are not trusted.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:1:1.hebrew: קים לי בנפשאי - ולא היתה ספיקא בידו, וטעות הוא, וכי אתני — אדעתא דהוא נצח אתני, ולא גמר ואקני. אבל תולה בדעת יונו — ספיקא הוא בידו אי נצח, ואפ"ה אתני מספיקא; הלכך, גמר ומקני:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:1:1.english: I am certain of myself - And there was no doubt in his mind, and it is an error; and when he stipulated [the wager], he stipulated with the assumption that he would win, and he did not wholeheartedly resolve to transfer [ownership]. But one who makes it dependent on the mind of his pigeon — it is uncertain to him whether he will win, and even so he stipulated despite the uncertainty; therefore, he wholeheartedly resolves to transfer [ownership].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:20:1.hebrew: לא לדינא - דלדינא מודינא דפסולין, משום דלא גמירי דינא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:20:1.english: No, with regard to judgment - For with regard to judgment, I concede that they are disqualified, because they have not learned the law.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:22:1.hebrew: דלא שכיחי בישוב - ולא ראו ולא שמעו עסקי דין בין אדם לחבירו, אי קבלינהו עלויה — לא מצי למיהדר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:22:1.english: Who do not frequent the settled area - And [therefore] have neither seen nor heard legal proceedings between a person and his fellow; [yet] if [a litigant] accepted them upon himself, he cannot retract.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:23:1.english: An ordinary shepherd - [One regarding whom] we have not yet seen that his animals entered into the fields of others.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:23:2.english: An ordinary [tax] collector is fit - Until we hear about him that he takes extra.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:24:1.hebrew: כי הוה חזי - אבוה דר' זירא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:24:1.english: When he would see - [This refers to] the father of Rabbi Zeira.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:24:2.english: The rabbis - [Who were] from among the inhabitants of the city.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:24:3.hebrew: אמר לך עמי בא בחדריך - דלא נחזינא בך ריש נהרא, שהוא שר העיר, ורואה שרבים יושבי העיר ושואל ממון הרבה לכל שנה. והוא היה מיקל עליהם המס ומדחה את שר העיר, לאמר שיושביה מועטין ואין ממי לגבות:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:24:3.english: He said: “Come, my people, enter into your chambers” - So that the Reish Nahara, who is the governor of the city, will not see you and see that the inhabitants of the city are numerous, and demand much money each year. And he would lighten the tax upon them and turn away the governor of the city, saying that its inhabitants are few and there is no one from whom to collect.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:24:4.hebrew: נכיס אבא לפום ברא - ישחוט את האב לפני הבן, כלומר: יגבה מהן ממון:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:24:4.english: [He will] slaughter the father before the son - He will slaughter the father before the son; that is to say, he will collect money from them:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:2:1.hebrew: בנקשא תליא מילתא - שיש לו דפין של עץ מנקשין זו לזו, והיונה שומעת קולן ומכרת שבעלה מזרזה, וממהרת לעוף:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:2:1.english: The matter depends on the knocking - That he has wooden boards knocking against one another, and the pigeon hears their sound and recognizes that its owner is urging it on, and hastens to fly.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:2:2.hebrew: ה"ג - אנא ידענא בנקשא טפי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:2:2.english: This is the text we read: “I know how to knock better.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:3:1.hebrew: פספסין - שברי עצים, והן מרלי"ש בלע"ז:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:3:1.english: Pispasim - Pieces of wood; and they are merles [gaming pieces] in Old French.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:3:2.hebrew: אפילו קליפי אגוזים - שאין עשויין לכך, ואקראי בעלמא הוא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:3:2.english: Even nutshells - Which are not made for this, and it is merely incidental.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:5:1.hebrew: דאפילו לנכרי - שישתכח שם ריבית מפיהם, דתו ודאי לא הדרי לקלקולייהו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:5:1.english: That even to a gentile - So that the mention of interest will be forgotten from their mouths, for then they will certainly not return to their corrupt practice.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:6:1.english: Those who incite the pigeons - They provoke them against one another to fight.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:6:2.english: Even a domesticated animal and a wild animal - For [this] is not a common thing.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:6:3.english: Their fixtures - These are boards with which they urge [the animals] on.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:6:4.hebrew: אפילו במדבר - דלא שכיחי יונים דיישוב. והאי פירושא, ללישנא דארא נקיט ליה, ולא מגופא דברייתא היא. וללישנא ד"אי תקדמה יונך ליון", איכא לפרושי חזרה גמורה: דהא אפילו בחנם נמי לא עבדו, כדפרישית גבי קוביא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:6:4.english: Even in the wilderness - As pigeons of an inhabited area are not found [there]. And this explanation [the Gemara] adopted according to the version of ara [luring pigeons], and it is not from the body of the baraita itself. And according to the version of “if your pigeon outpaces [my] pigeon,” one can explain “complete repentance” [as meaning]: that they do not do [it] even for free, as I explained regarding dice.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:7:1.hebrew: ויבדלו - שלא ישאו ויתנו בפירותיהן, ויפקרו גנותיהן לעניים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:7:1.english: And they refrain - That they do not do business with its produce, and they declare their gardens ownerless for the poor.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:8:1.hebrew: לא חזרת דברים - לומר: ״לא נוסיף עוד״, אלא חזרה הנכרת — שיפזרו פירות שביעית שבגנותיהן לעניים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:8:1.english: Not verbal repentance - To [merely] say, "We will not do so again," but rather a discernible repentance — that they distribute the produce of the Sabbatical Year in their gardens to the poor.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:9:1.english: This is how you find [a case involving] an animal - For it is possible that he trains it to run when it hears his voice.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:9:2.hebrew: בת הכי היא - שתביא בהמות הבר לביתה עמה, והלא ירדפוה החיות:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25b:9:2.english: Is it capable of this - That it would bring wild animals to its home with it? But would the wild beasts not pursue it?

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 25b:13:1.hebrew: אי נמי מפני דרכי שלום - תימה: למ"ד מפריחי יונים — ארא, א"כ מעיקרא נמי פסולים מפני דרכי שלום! וי"ל, דהא דאמרי' "מפני דרכי שלום" קאי אלישנא ד"תקדמיה יונך ליון":
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 25b:13:1.english: "Alternatively, on account of the ways of peace" - This is difficult: According to the one who says [that] "pigeon flyers" [refers to] an ara [decoy bird], if so, initially [people] were also disqualified on account of the ways of peace! And one can say: That which we say, "on account of the ways of peace," follows the opinion of: "If your pigeon reaches before [my] pigeon."

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 25b:14:1.hebrew: מעיקרא סבור דמי קיהיב - וא"ת: וליפסול מדאורייתא, דקא עבר אלאו ד"לא תחמוד"? וי"ל: ד"לא תחמוד" משמע דלא יהיב דמי, וכי יהיב דמי — ליכא לאו דחמוד כלל. וא"ת: והא אמרינן בפ"ק דבבא מציעא (דף ה:): "לא תחמוד בלא דמי משמע להו"? משמע: לאינשי דווקא הוא דמשתמע כך, אבל הם טועים, ד"לא תחמוד" הוו אפי' בדיהיב דמי! וי"ל: "דמשמע להו" דקאמר, ר"ל נמי דכן הוא האמת. ועי"ל: דהכא הכי קאמר: דמי קא יהבי והיו מפייסים אותם עד שיאמרו "רוצה אני", אם כן לא עברי אלאו ד"לא תחמוד"; כיון דחזו דשקלי בעל כרחייהו ולא היו חוששין אם יתפייסו — פסלינהו:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 25b:14:1.english: "Initially they assumed he pays money" - And if you say: Let him be disqualified by Torah law, as he transgresses the negative commandment of "You shall not covet"? And one can say: "You shall not covet" implies when one does not pay money, but when one pays money, there is no negative commandment of coveting at all. And if you say: But don't we say in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (5b): "People understand [the prohibition of] 'You shall not covet' [as applying only] without payment"? This implies: It is specifically to [ordinary] people that it seems this way, but they are mistaken, as "You shall not covet" applies even when one pays money! And one can say: When it says "it seems to them," it means to say that this is also the truth. And further it can be said: Here, this is what it means: They would pay money and would appease them until they said, "I am willing"; if so, they did not transgress the negative commandment of "You shall not covet." Once they saw that they take [the items] against their will and were unconcerned whether they would be appeased, they disqualified them.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 25b:18:1.hebrew: מגדלי איתמר - פי': בהמה דקה אסור לגדל, אפי' בבית, משום ישוב ארץ ישראל, דילמא אתי לרעותן בשדות; ובהמה גסה מותר לגדל בבית, ולא גזרו בה חכמים משום דצריך לחרישה, ואין יכולין לעמוד בהאי גזירה. וא"ת: והא מתניתין היא במרובה (ב"ק דף עט: ושם): "אין מגדלין בהמה דקה בארץ ישראל", משמע דווקא דקה, אבל גסה מגדלין! וי"ל: דאי מההיא, הוה אמינא: ה"ה גסה, ודקה דנקט — לאשמועינן חידוש דסיפא: דאפי' דקה אינו אסור אלא בארץ ישראל דווקא, אבל לא בסוריא, דכיבוש יחיד לא הוי כיבוש; קמ"ל:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 25b:18:1.english: "It was stated with regard to [those who] raise" - Explanation: It is forbidden to raise small livestock even in a house, due to the settlement of Eretz Yisrael, lest one come to graze them in the fields. But large livestock is permitted to raise in a house, and the Sages did not decree against it because it is needed for plowing, and they would not be able to abide by such a decree. And if you say: But this is [already] a Mishnah in [the chapter entitled] Merubah (Bava Kamma 79b and elsewhere): "One may not raise small livestock in Eretz Yisrael," which implies specifically small [livestock], but large [livestock] one may raise! And one can say: That if [learned only] from that [Mishnah], I would have said that the same applies to large [livestock], and [the reason] that it stated "small" was to teach us the novel ruling of the latter clause: that even small [livestock] is forbidden only in Eretz Yisrael specifically, but not in Syria, as an individual conquest is not considered a [valid] conquest; [therefore, Rava] teaches us [that large livestock is permitted to raise in Eretz Yisrael].

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 25b:23:1.hebrew: סתם גבאי כשר - פ"ה: והא דהוסיפו הגבאין והמוכסין בדחזו דשקלי יתירתא — וקא אתי לאשמועינן, דאע"ג שהחזיר הגבאי והמוכס — פסול; דלא דמי לשאר גזלנים שהחזירו דכשרים, דהאי לא ידע למאן נהדר; ועוד, כיון דעדיין הם עוסקין בגבאות ובמכס — חשודים לחזור לקלקולם:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 25b:23:1.english: An ordinary tax collector is fit - Rashi explained: And that which [the Sages] added the tax collectors and the customs officials [only] when they saw that they take extra — [the baraita] comes to teach us that even though the tax collector and the customs official returned [the overcharge], he is disqualified; for he is not like other robbers who returned [what they stole], who are fit [to testify], for this one does not know to whom to return [it]; and furthermore, since they are still engaged in tax collecting and customs collecting, they are suspected of reverting to their corrupt ways.
